vemd/3/p0.context: System note 'VEMD: Vehicle and Engine Management Display', section 'The pages', paragraph
vemd/3/p0.text: FLI (First Limitation Indicator) is the default summary page. If any FLI parameter becomes invalid, the ENGINE page displays automatically instead, showing the same parameters on independent scales. The VEHICLE page shows aircraft-level parameters and is automatically replaced by the FLIGHT REPORT page once the VEMD detects engine shutdown with NR below 70 rpm — a flight number (auto-incrementing), flight time (Ng > 60% after start to Ng < 50% at shutdown), generator and free-turbine cycle counts, and a yellow message area if a discrepancy was detected during the flight.
vemd/3/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
vemd/3/p0.note: RFM Section 7.4 p.6/10 (FLI page note, FLIGHT REPORT page): FLI->ENGINE page on invalid parameter, independent scales; FLIGHT REPORT replaces VEHICLE page at engine shutdown + NR<70rpm; flight number, flight time (Ng>60% to Ng<50%), generator/free-turbine cycles, yellow message area. Confirmed verbatim.

vemd/3/p1.context: System note 'VEMD: Vehicle and Engine Management Display', section 'The pages', paragraph
vemd/3/p1.text: The Engine Power Check (EPC) page runs in three phases — value stabilization, a more restrictive stabilization, then margin computation — and its second page reports the result across six parameters (Ng, Nf, T4, Hp/Zp, Tq, OAT) with the positive or negative differences in T4 and torque.
vemd/3/p1.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
vemd/3/p1.note: RFM Section 7.4 p.7/8 (ENGINE POWER CHECK page): 3 phases (stabilization, more restrictive stabilization, margin computation), 6 parameters (Ng, Nf, t4, Hp/Zp, Tq, OAT) with t4/torque differences. Confirmed verbatim.

vemd/3/p2.context: System note 'VEMD: Vehicle and Engine Management Display', section 'The pages', paragraph
vemd/3/p2.text: The PERFORMANCE page computes takeoff weights (IGE and OGE) from equipped empty weight, crew weight (default 80 kg at power-up), and payload (defaults to the maximum internal takeoff weight), combined with Hp and OAT — both of which can be manually adjusted for mission planning; changing Hp automatically decreases OAT per the standard atmosphere law. IGE/OGE values below the aircraft's all-up weight display in yellow; if actual hover performance exceeds the demonstrated envelope on the HIGE/HOGE charts, IGE/OGE shows in white with the corresponding weight in yellow instead.
vemd/3/p2.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
vemd/3/p2.note: RFM Section 7.4 p.8/9 (PERFORMANCE page): EEW, crew default 80kg, payload defaults to max internal TO weight, Hp/OAT adjustable with standard atmosphere law, yellow/white IGE-OGE display logic. Confirmed verbatim.

afcs/0/p0.text: The SFIM 85 T 31 holds pitch, roll, and yaw attitudes and heading as set by the pilot, with four additional modes: A/S (holds present airspeed), ALT (holds present pressure altitude), HDG (acquires and holds the HSI-selected heading), and T/C (automatic yaw/roll coordination in turns).

afcs/0/p1.context: System note 'AFCS: SFIM 85 T 31 (3-Axis)', section 'What it is', paragraph
afcs/0/p1.text: The installation: an AFCS computer fed by a vertical gyro, the HSI, a directional gyro and flux valve, an air data unit, a yaw pedal displacement detector, and a lateral accelerometer (sideslip detector); a yaw pedal friction adjustment system; three series actuators (one per channel, each with its own 'channel disengaged' galvanometer); two parallel trim actuators (pitch and roll) tied to the artificial-load-release (trim release) function; an AFCS warning and monitoring panel; a control panel with P/R/Y/ALT/A-S/HDG/T-C/MONIT engagement buttons (each shows green ON when engaged); and a dedicated static inverter (115/26 VAC, 400 Hz) for AC power.

afcs/2/note.context: System note 'AFCS: SFIM 85 T 31 (3-Axis)', section 'Flying modes', table note
afcs/2/note.text: Hands off, the AFCS holds attitude. With the cyclic trim released, it operates purely as a damper — the trim actuators are inhibited and the series actuators counteract disturbances within their limited authority. Cyclic beep trim changes the attitude reference directly. On yaw: 'feet off' holds present heading within the channel's authority; working the pedals shifts the heading reference; after a deliberate heading change, once turn rate drops below 1.5°/sec the new heading is captured and 'feet off' flying resumes.
afcs/2/note.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
afcs/2/note.note: RFM SUP.16 p.10 (4.3.1.1/4.3.1.2 flying modes): hands-off holds attitude, trim released = damper (trim actuators inhibited, series actuators counteract within authority), cyclic beep trim changes reference; feet-off holds heading, pedals shift reference, <1.5°/sec captures new heading. power-plant/0/p0.context: System note 'Power Plant and Engine Control', section 'The engine', paragraph
power-plant/0/p0.text: A single Turbomeca (Safran) Arriel 2B1, a 650 kW (870 hp) class turboshaft, in its own fireproof compartment aft of the MGB and above the rear cargo hold, connected to the MGB by a shaft between two flexible couplings. It is a modular free-wheel engine built from five independent modules: the axial compressor module (single stage, with a bleed valve), the gas generator module (centrifugal compressor, annular combustion chamber, single-stage gas generator turbine), the free turbine module, the reduction gear module (steps the free turbine down from 39,158 rpm to 6,000 rpm), and the output shaft module (drives the MGB and the accessory couplings).
power-plant/0/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
power-plant/0/p0.note: RFM Complementary Section 7.7 p.1: Turbomeca Arriel 2B1, 650kW (870hp) class, fireproof compartment aft of MGB above rear cargo, 5 modules. Confirmed verbatim.

power-plant/1/p1.context: System note 'Power Plant and Engine Control', section 'The FADEC', paragraph
power-plant/1/p1.text: The EECU also handles automatic starting with T4 overlimit prevention, proportional Nf control with a rotor-noise-reduction feature, surge and flame-out protection during transients, bleed-valve monitoring, Ng and torque overlimit protection, failure detection and indication, the Engine Power Check, and Ng/Nf cycle counting. Post-MOD 07-20060/07-20061 it adds automatic engine shutdown on an Nf overspeed above 120% (NR 463 rpm), closing the main metering valve; restart capability is unaffected.
power-plant/1/p1.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
power-plant/1/p1.note: RFM Section 7.8 p.3 (FADEC functions list): automatic starting/t4 overlimit prevention, proportional Nf control w/ noise reduction, surge/flame-out protection, bleed valve monitoring, Ng/torque overlimit protection, failure detection, EPC, cycle counting, post-MOD Nf>120% (NR=463rpm) auto shutdown. Confirmed verbatim.

power-plant/2/p0.context: System note 'Power Plant and Engine Control', section 'FADEC power — and why it survives an electrical failure', paragraph
power-plant/2/p0.text: Once gas generator speed is established (Ng > 60%), normal engine running is independent of the helicopter electrical system: the FADEC is then fed by an alternator with two independent channels driven by the gas generator. Helicopter 28 VDC is still needed for the starting sequence and the monitoring system, and as a back-up source for the EECU's fuel control section.
power-plant/2/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
power-plant/2/p0.note: RFM Section 7.8 p.3 (FADEC power supplies): independent of helicopter electrical once Ng>60%, alternator w/ 2 channels driven by gas generator; helicopter 28VDC needed for starting/monitoring/back-up. Confirmed verbatim.

power-plant/3/r0.text: Level: 1; Indication: GOV flashing (at idle, starting, or engine stopped); Effect: No effect on engine control — loss of redundancy only. Reset the FADEC before start (battery OFF/ON); refer to Section 3
power-plant/3/r0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
power-plant/3/r0.note: RFM Section 7.8 p.5 (FADEC failures Level 1): flashing GOV at idle/start/stopped, no effect on control, redundancy loss, reset before start. Confirmed verbatim.

power-plant/3/r1.context: System note 'Power Plant and Engine Control', table 'FADEC failure levels', one row (columns ['Level', 'Indication', 'Effect'])
power-plant/3/r1.text: Level: 2; Indication: GOV steady; Effect: Degraded but protected engine control, or the back-up governing system out of its neutral position — loss of accuracy, loss of power check; refer to Section 3
power-plant/3/r1.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
power-plant/3/r1.note: RFM Section 7.8 p.5 (Level 2): steady GOV, degraded but protected control, loss of accuracy/power check. Confirmed verbatim.

power-plant/3/r2.context: System note 'Power Plant and Engine Control', table 'FADEC failure levels', one row (columns ['Level', 'Indication', 'Effect'])
power-plant/3/r2.text: Level: 3; Indication: GOV (total FADEC failure); Effect: The FADEC main metering valve is frozen at its last computed value, the back-up system activates automatically, automatic start is impossible; refer to Section 3
power-plant/3/r2.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
power-plant/3/r2.note: RFM Section 7.8 p.5 (Level 3): total FADEC failure, valve frozen at last value, back-up auto-activates, auto start impossible. Confirmed verbatim.

power-plant/4/p0.context: System note 'Power Plant and Engine Control', section 'The EBCAU back-up governor', paragraph
power-plant/4/p0.text: The fuel governor back-up system is an electronic computer — the Engine Back-up Control Ancillary Unit (EBCAU), ASU card No. 3 — completely independent of the FADEC. On detection of a total FADEC failure it takes over engine fuel governing immediately, holding Nf between 388 and 400 rpm. It also runs on the ground for a maintenance test, after which the back-up valve returns to neutral.
power-plant/4/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
power-plant/4/p0.note: RFM Section 7.8 p.6 (Fuel governor back-up system): EBCAU electronic computer, independent of FADEC, controls Nf 388-400 rpm, activated after total FADEC failure, ground maintenance test with return to neutral. Confirmed verbatim.

power-plant/4/note.context: System note 'Power Plant and Engine Control', section 'The EBCAU back-up governor', table note
power-plant/4/note.text: In-flight engine power reduction using the twist grip is prohibited except for engine failure training and the emergency procedures that call for it. The twist grip normally sits in the FLIGHT detent; IDLE is used on the ground. Heating and demisting must not be used above the engine maximum continuous rating (Ng or T4).
power-plant/4/note.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
power-plant/4/note.note: RFM Section 2.1 (forbidden list, twist grip power reduction) and Section 4.3/4.8 (twist grip IDLE on ground / FLIGHT for flight) and Section 2.4 §4 (heating/demisting restriction). Confirmed verbatim/cross-referenced.

fuel-system/0/p1.context: System note 'Fuel System', section 'What it is', paragraph
fuel-system/0/p1.text: Total capacity is 540 litres (427 kg). Usable fuel is 538.7 litres / 425.6 kg (938 lb) with the standard tank, or 538 litres / 425 kg (937 lb) with the crash-resistant tank.
fuel-system/0/p1.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
fuel-system/0/p1.note: RFM Section 7.1 p.3 (2.4 FUEL): total capacity 540l (427kg), usable 538.7l/425.6kg (938lb) standard tank or 538l/425kg (937lb) crash-resistant tank. Confirmed verbatim.

fuel-system/2/p0.context: System note 'Fuel System', section 'Engine supply side', paragraph
fuel-system/2/p0.text: The engine LP pump draws fuel up through the filter to the HP pump, helped at the circuit entry by an ejector fed from the HP pump that primes the LP pump. The filter carries an electrical pre-clogging indicator, a by-pass valve with a visual indicator, and a low-pressure detector. The fuel is warmed by the combined engine fuel/oil filter assembly — enough to allow operation down to −20°C with no anti-ice additive in the fuel — then delivered to the FADEC hydro-mechanical unit.
fuel-system/2/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
fuel-system/2/p0.note: RFM Section 7.8 p.1 (3 ENGINE FUEL SUPPLY SYSTEM): LP pump draws through filter to HP pump, ejector primes LP pump, filter has pre-clogging indicator/bypass valve/low-pressure detector, heated by fuel/oil filter assembly (-20°C without additive), delivered to hydro-mechanical unit. Confirmed verbatim.

fuel-system/2/p1.context: System note 'Fuel System', section 'Engine supply side', paragraph
fuel-system/2/p1.text: From the hydro-mechanical unit the fuel passes a shut-off solenoid valve (the means of shutting the engine down) and a pressurizing valve before reaching the main injector and injection wheel. A three-way electrovalve feeds two starting injectors during the start; once the start sequence ends they are fed with P3 air to prevent carbonisation. On shutdown a purge valve drains the fuel left in the main injection system.
fuel-system/2/p1.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
fuel-system/2/p1.note: RFM Section 7.8 p.1: shut-off solenoid valve, pressurizing valve, main injector/injection wheel, three-way electrovalve to starting injectors then P3 air post-start, purge valve on shutdown. Confirmed verbatim.

fuel-system/3/note.context: System note 'Fuel System', section 'Controls and monitoring', table note
fuel-system/3/note.text: Approved normal fuels include F34/JP-8, F35/Jet A-1, Jet A, F43/F44 (JP-5), and Chinese Jet Fuel No. 3. If the fuel contains no freezing inhibitor and OAT is below −20°C, an anti-icing additive is mandatory. Fuels not listed in Section 2.5 must not be used.
fuel-system/3/note.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
fuel-system/3/note.note: RFM Section 2.5 (NORMAL FUELS table + additives): F34/F35/JetA/F43/F44/Chinese Jet Fuel No.3; anti-ice additive mandatory OAT<-20°C without inhibitor; unlisted fuels excluded. Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/0/p0.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', section 'Single hydraulic system — the baseline', paragraph
hydraulic-system/0/p0.text: Three main rotor servos (one longitudinal, two lateral) plus a tail rotor servo provide hydraulic assistance, fed by a single constant-flow gear pump belt-driven off the engine power drive shaft near the MGB input. Total fluid volume is 3 liters (0.79 US gal) to the reservoir's max mark; the regulator holds 40 bars (580 psi).
hydraulic-system/0/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/0/p0.note: RFM Section 7.10 p.1 (1 GENERAL): 3 main rotor servos (1 longitudinal, 2 lateral) + tail rotor servo, single constant-flow gear pump belt-driven off engine power drive shaft near MGB input, 3L (0.79 US gal) to max mark, regulator 40 bars (580 psi). Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/1/p0.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', section 'SAMM vs. Dunlop servos', paragraph
hydraulic-system/1/p0.text: The AS350 can be fitted with lateral servos from either supplier, and they behave differently at the unpowered/powered transition. SAMM servos include an input clearance locking system that reduces control freeplay in bypass mode — but because the two lateral servos' unlock pressures can differ slightly (unequal control loads, or manufacturing tolerance in the unlock threshold), pressurizing the system with the collective locked can produce a large, sudden cyclic movement to one side; the pilot should hold the cyclic firmly (about 5 daN / 11 lbf) through pressurization to prevent it, and expect a small cyclic movement on any powered/unpowered transition in flight. Dunlop servos have no input locking device and aren't subject to this asymmetric-unlock behavior, though a small cyclic movement on transition can still occur.
hydraulic-system/1/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/1/p0.note: RFM Section 7.10 p.3 (2.3 MAIN ROTOR SERVO): SAMM input clearance locking system, asymmetric unlock pressure risk, ~5 daN (11lbf) hold, Dunlop no locking device, small transition movement still possible for both. Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/2/p0.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', section 'Pre-flight tests and what they check', paragraph
hydraulic-system/2/p0.text: The accumulator test (HYD TEST / ACCU TST, pressed) checks that the accumulators still provide assistance if the hydraulic power system fails — i.e. no significant leaks — flagged by the HYDR light and Gong. The hydraulic cut-off test (collective switch to OFF) checks the main servo dump electrovalves that the emergency procedures rely on; setting cut-off depressurizes all three accumulators simultaneously via their electrovalves. Repressurization on returning the switch to ON should take about 3 seconds to reach nominal pressure — this becomes the diagnostic for accumulator health (see Abnormal Operation below).
hydraulic-system/2/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/2/p0.note: RFM Section 7.10 p.5 (3 NORMAL OPERATION): accumulator test checks no significant leaks (HYDR+Gong), cut-off test checks main servo dump electrovalves (depressurizes 3 accumulators simultaneously), repressurization ~2-3s normal. Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/3/r0.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', table 'Abnormal operation — single system', one row (columns ['Situation', 'Detail'])
hydraulic-system/3/r0.text: Situation: Accumulator malfunction; Detail: Normal repressurization after a cut-off test is 2–3 s; less than 1 s or more than 4 s means at least one accumulator is faulty — maintenance is required before flight
hydraulic-system/3/r0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/3/r0.note: RFM Section 7.10 p.6 (4.1 ACCUMULATOR MALFUNCTION): normal 2-3s, <1s or >4s means faulty accumulator, maintenance required. Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/3/r1.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', table 'Abnormal operation — single system', one row (columns ['Situation', 'Detail'])
hydraulic-system/3/r1.text: Situation: Hydraulic pressure loss; Detail: HYDR + Gong, controls still powered by the accumulators. Average time to reach the recommended safety speed (40–60 kt) from VNE or hover is under 30 seconds if the accumulators are properly serviced. Cut off hydraulics as soon as the safety speed is reached — even if the accumulators still have assistance left — to depressurize all three simultaneously and avoid an asymmetric lateral-accumulator depletion
hydraulic-system/3/r1.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/3/r1.note: RFM Section 7.10 p.6 (4.2 HYDRAULIC PRESSURE LOSS): HYDR+Gong, accumulators still power controls, <30s to safety speed if serviced, cut off at safety speed even with assistance left to avoid asymmetric depletion. Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/3/note.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', section 'Abnormal operation — single system', table note
hydraulic-system/3/note.text: At the 40–60 kt safety speed with collective near neutral (~40% torque), expect to hold roughly 4 daN (9 lbf) left lateral cyclic and 5 daN (11 lbf) forward longitudinal cyclic continuously. In a running landing around 10 kt, forward longitudinal force can reach 17 daN (38 lbf) for under 30 seconds. In a hover, expect up to 5 daN (11 lbf) changing rapidly in direction — high workload, and prolonging flight after a hydraulic failure isn't recommended due to fatigue. Other malfunctions (individual component failures rather than a clean pressure loss) can show unusual symptoms: lateral loads pulling LEFT (requiring a RIGHT pull to counter), feedback that can be felt immediately on failure with little or no delay, or a cut-off switch that doesn't fully dump pressure — if the switch itself is inoperative, forces should still normalize once the accumulators deplete naturally, up to roughly 15 daN (34 lbf) lateral and 17 daN (38 lbf) longitudinal at the extremes of the speed envelope.
hydraulic-system/3/note.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/3/note.note: FIXED: 'feedback that varies unusually with airspeed' replaced - the RFM's actual second bullet (Section 7.10 p.8, 4.3 OTHER MALFUNCTIONS) is about immediate feedback with little/no delay after failure, not airspeed-dependent variation. Force values (4 daN/9lbf lateral, 5 daN/11lbf longitudinal at 40-60kt/~40% torque; 17 daN/38lbf running landing; 5 daN/11lbf hover; up to 15 daN/34lbf lateral and 17 daN/38lbf longitudinal at speed extremes) all confirmed verbatim against Section 7.10 p.6-8.

hydraulic-system/4/p0.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', section 'Dual hydraulic system (optional)', paragraph
hydraulic-system/4/p0.text: Two fully independent circuits share the same main-rotor architecture — each with its own reservoir (2 liters / 0.53 US gal to max level), gear pump, and regulator at 35 bars (507 psi), each supplying the three dual-body main rotor servos. Only the RH circuit additionally supplies the accumulator, load compensator, and yaw servo. The two pumps are driven differently — one gear-driven directly off the MGB, the other belt-driven off the engine power drive shaft — so a single drive-path fault can't take out both.
hydraulic-system/4/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/4/p0.note: RFM SUP.23 p.1 (1 GENERAL): two independent circuits, same main-rotor architecture, 2L (0.53 US gal) reservoir each, 35 bar (507 psi) regulator, RH circuit also feeds accumulator/load compensator/yaw servo, pumps driven differently (one MGB-gear-driven, one belt-driven off engine). Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/4/p1.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', section 'Dual hydraulic system (optional)', paragraph
hydraulic-system/4/p1.text: A yaw hydraulic switch on the collective isolates the yaw circuit independently. SERVO TEST checks for servo distributor jamming; HYD TEST/ACCU TST runs the yaw servo accumulator test. Post-modification 07-4622, separate HYD1 and HYD2 caution lights (rather than one shared HYDR) identify which circuit has lost pressure — HYD2 also flashes if the yaw cut-off switch is OFF. A SERVO light indicates distributor seizure; a LIMIT light means the maximum lateral servo load has been reached.
hydraulic-system/4/p1.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/4/p1.note: RFM SUP.23 p.1 (Commands and controls): yaw servo hydraulic switch, SERVO TEST/SERVO TST, HYD TEST/ACCU TST, post-MOD 07-4622 HYD1/HYD2 lights (HYD2 flashes if yaw cut-off OFF), SERVO light (distributor seizure), LIMIT light (max lateral servo load). Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/5/r0.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', table 'Dual system — malfunction logic', one row (columns ['Indication', 'Meaning', 'Action'])
hydraulic-system/5/r0.text: Indication: HYD1 or HYD2 + SERVO; Meaning: Pressure loss in the corresponding circuit; Action: Avoid abrupt maneuvers, bank <30°, IAS below 110 kt (or VNE if less); one remaining circuit allows continued safe flight and landing
hydraulic-system/5/r0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/5/r0.note: RFM SUP.23 p.6 (3.2.2 hydraulic alarms, HYD1/HYD2+SERVO): avoid abrupt maneuvers, bank<30°, IAS<110kt or VNE if less, one remaining circuit allows safe flight/landing. Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/5/r1.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', table 'Dual system — malfunction logic', one row (columns ['Indication', 'Meaning', 'Action'])
hydraulic-system/5/r1.text: Indication: HYD2 + LIMIT possibly present; Meaning: Loss of the RH circuit — tail rotor control hydraulic power is lost; Action: Do not press HYD TEST/ACCU TST — this would discharge the yaw load compensator and significantly increase right pedal loads. Land as soon as practicable
hydraulic-system/5/r1.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/5/r1.note: RFM SUP.23 p.6: HYD2/LIMIT = RH circuit loss, tail rotor hydraulic power lost, do not press HYD TEST/ACCU TST (discharges yaw load compensator), land as soon as practicable. Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/5/r2.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', table 'Dual system — malfunction logic', one row (columns ['Indication', 'Meaning', 'Action'])
hydraulic-system/5/r2.text: Indication: SERVO alone; Meaning: Distributor valve jamming on a main servo unit; Action: Land as soon as practicable
hydraulic-system/5/r2.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/5/r2.note: RFM SUP.23 p.6: SERVO alone = distributor valve jamming, land as soon as practicable. Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/5/r3.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', table 'Dual system — malfunction logic', one row (columns ['Indication', 'Meaning', 'Action'])
hydraulic-system/5/r3.text: Indication: LIMIT alone; Meaning: Main servo unit at max load, in high-speed cruise or steep maneuvers; Action: Reduce power (collective) and speed/load factor (cyclic); continue flight
hydraulic-system/5/r3.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/5/r3.note: RFM SUP.23 p.6: LIMIT alone = main servo max load in high-speed cruise/steep maneuvers, reduce power/speed, continue flight. Confirmed verbatim.

hydraulic-system/6/p0.context: System note 'Hydraulic System — Single and Dual', section 'Loss of tail rotor control (dual system)', paragraph
hydraulic-system/6/p0.text: Symptom: pedals jammed or ineffective — tail rotor thrust can't be controlled with the pedals. Set IAS to 70 kt in level flight, hydraulic cut-off switch OFF, then press ACCU TST for 2 seconds to depressurize the load compensator. Fly a shallow approach with a slight left sideslip onto a suitable running-landing area — the sideslip reduces progressively as airspeed decreases and collective is applied to cushion the landing. A right crosswind component makes the landing easier. Below 20 kt and especially near the ground, a go-around may be impossible due to loss of vertical fin efficiency.
hydraulic-system/6/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
hydraulic-system/6/p0.note: RFM SUP.23 p.4 (3.1 LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR CONTROL): set IAS 70kt, hydraulic cut-off OFF, ACCU TST 2s, shallow approach slight left sideslip, running landing, RH wind easier, <20kt near ground go-around may be impossible (vertical fin efficiency). Confirmed verbatim.

electrical-power-systems/0/p0.context: System note 'Electrical Power Systems', section 'DC power sources', paragraph
electrical-power-systems/0/p0.text: Three sources feed the 28 VDC network: a starter-generator (150 A, 200 A optional) on the engine accessory gearbox, a 15 A/h battery in the RH rear cargo bay (an optional second battery may be fitted), and a 28 V external power unit (EPU) receptacle rated 400 A max. All three connect through the Electrical Master Box (EMB), which regulates the starter-generator, connects power sources to the network via line contactors, handles distribution and fault protection, and interfaces with the indicating/control/monitoring system.
electrical-power-systems/0/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
electrical-power-systems/0/p0.note: RFM Section 7.11 p.1/2 (1.1 GENERAL, EMB functions): starter-generator (150A/200A optional), 15A/h battery + optional second, 28V EPU receptacle 400A max, EMB regulates/connects/distributes/interfaces. Confirmed verbatim.

electrical-power-systems/1/r0.context: System note 'Electrical Power Systems', table 'Coupling logic', one row (columns ['Source', 'Couples when', 'Isolates when'])
electrical-power-systems/1/r0.text: Source: EPU; Couples when: 28 VDC available at the plug, MASTER SW/EMER SW normal (ON), EXT PWR BATT/BAT-EPU pressed; Isolates when: Disconnected — battery and generator stay isolated from the DC system until then
electrical-power-systems/1/r0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
electrical-power-systems/1/r0.note: RFM Section 7.11 p.7 (EPU coupling): 28VDC at plug, MASTER SW/EMER SW ON, EXT PWR BATT/BAT-EPU pressed; battery+generator isolated until EPU disconnected. Confirmed verbatim.

electrical-power-systems/1/r1.context: System note 'Electrical Power Systems', table 'Coupling logic', one row (columns ['Source', 'Couples when', 'Isolates when'])
electrical-power-systems/1/r1.text: Source: Battery; Couples when: 28 VDC not available at EPU plug, MASTER SW/EMER SW normal (ON), EXT PWR BATT/BAT-EPU pressed; Isolates when: Automatically via EPU power, or manually via MASTER SW/EXT PWR BATT off
electrical-power-systems/1/r1.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
electrical-power-systems/1/r1.note: RFM Section 7.11 p.8 (Battery coupling, pre/post-MOD): no 28VDC at EPU plug, MASTER SW or EMER SW ON, EXT PWR BATT or BAT/EPU pressed; isolates via EPU power or manually. Confirmed verbatim.

electrical-power-systems/1/r2.context: System note 'Electrical Power Systems', table 'Coupling logic', one row (columns ['Source', 'Couples when', 'Isolates when'])
electrical-power-systems/1/r2.text: Source: Generator; Couples when: Engine running, no EPU power, MASTER SW/EMER SW normal (ON), GEN/GENE switched ON, generator voltage exceeds battery voltage by ≥0.5 V; Isolates when: Manually (GEN/GENE off, or MASTER SW/EMER SW off), or automatically via EPU power, reverse current battery→generator, generator voltage >31.5 V, or CRANK activation — GENE light comes on
electrical-power-systems/1/r2.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
electrical-power-systems/1/r2.note: RFM Section 7.11 p.9 (Generator system): engine running, no EPU power, MASTER SW/EMER SW ON, GEN/GENE ON, voltage exceeds battery by >=0.5V; isolates manually or automatically (EPU power, reverse current, >31.5V, CRANK), GENE light on. Confirmed verbatim.

electrical-power-systems/2/p0.context: System note 'Electrical Power Systems', section 'The direct battery bus-bar — what survives an emergency', paragraph
electrical-power-systems/2/p0.text: A direct battery linkage keeps a short list of vital consumers alive through a circuit failure or a MASTER SW/EMER SW disconnection. Pre-MOD 07-3273/3274: the transponder, the NR/Nf instrument, instrument lighting circuit 2, the crew's adjustable reading light, and the start-stop engine switch to FADEC (via a relay box). Post-MOD, two separate lists apply: the DCT/BATT pushbutton feeds the transponder, VHF1/NAV1, instrument lighting circuit 2, and one ICS power line — letting ground crew monitor radio and plan navigation on battery power alone without powering the whole aircraft — while a total electrical emergency (EMER SW set OFF) still leaves the NR/Nf instrument, the crew's adjustable spot light, and the start-stop engine switch to FADEC directly fed by the battery.
electrical-power-systems/2/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
electrical-power-systems/2/p0.note: FIXED: the app conflated two different post-MOD 07-3273/3274 consumer lists into one. RFM Section 7.11 p.8 (direct battery bus-bar via DCT/BATT, normal operation): Transponder, VHF1/NAV1, Instrument lighting circuit 2, one ICS power line. RFM Section 7.11 p.9 (separate list, after EMER SW set OFF in an electrical emergency): NR/Nf instrument, crew adjustable spot light, start-stop engine switch to FADEC. Pre-MOD list (unchanged, correct): Transponder, NR/Nf instrument, instrument lighting circuit 2, crew adjustable reading light, start-stop engine switch to FADEC.

electrical-power-systems/3/p0.context: System note 'Electrical Power Systems', section 'AC power — optional, for the AFCS and gyros', paragraph
electrical-power-systems/3/p0.text: AC power is only fitted when the aircraft carries an autopilot, gyroscopic instruments, or other equipment that needs it, supplied by a static inverter running off DC. Two capacities exist: a 250 VA system (115 VAC/150 VA plus 26 VAC/150 VA, max combined 250 VA) and a 10 VA system (26 VAC), both at 400 Hz. The inverter is switched on via the INVERT/INV pushbutton on the SCU; an amber INV caution light means the inverter isn't running, or the AC generating system has failed.
electrical-power-systems/3/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
electrical-power-systems/3/p0.note: RFM Section 7.11 p.10 (2 AC ELECTRICAL POWER): optional for AFCS/gyros, static inverter off DC, 250VA (115VAC/150VA+26VAC/150VA) and 10VA (26VAC) systems both 400Hz, INVERT/INV pushbutton on SCU, INV caution light. Confirmed verbatim.

ventilation-heating-demisting/1/p0.context: System note 'Ventilation, Heating and Demisting', section 'Heating and demisting', paragraph
ventilation-heating-demisting/1/p0.text: Heating and demisting work by mixing hot P2 air bled from the engine with outside air drawn from under the cabin floor. The mixture runs through two separate ducts — to heating outlets under the front seats, and to the demisting manifolds along the bottom of the front windscreen. Two manually operated valves on the P2 lines, on the cabin floor, open and regulate the warm-air distribution.
ventilation-heating-demisting/1/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
ventilation-heating-demisting/1/p0.note: RFM Section 7.13 p.2 (2 HEATING AND DEMISTING SYSTEM): P2 air mixed with outside air from under cabin floor, two ducts (heating under front seats, demisting at windscreen base), two manual valves on cabin floor. Confirmed verbatim.

ventilation-heating-demisting/1/note.context: System note 'Ventilation, Heating and Demisting', section 'Heating and demisting', table note
ventilation-heating-demisting/1/note.text: Use of heating and demisting is forbidden above the engine maximum continuous rating (Ng or T4) — the P2 bleed is a power cost the engine cannot carry at max continuous power. The sand filter note applies the same rule: heating and demisting must be off whenever the sand filter is active.
ventilation-heating-demisting/1/note.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
ventilation-heating-demisting/1/note.note: RFM Section 2.4 §4 (heating/demisting forbidden above max continuous rating) and Supplement 14 (sand filter rule) both confirmed verbatim; the P2-bleed-power-cost explanation is standard, physics-certain reasoning (bleed air is a parasitic engine load), not literal RFM text.

emergency-floatation-gear/0/p0.context: System note 'Emergency Floatation Gear', section 'What it is — and what it isn't', paragraph
emergency-floatation-gear/0/p0.text: This gear is approved for emergency use only — not for ditching under JAR 27 — to keep the rotorcraft sufficiently upright and trimmed for safe, orderly evacuation after an emergency water landing. It consists of two floatation units mounted parallel along each skid, inflated from two cylinders (one per float, each with a pressure indicator), a FLOAT ARM pushbutton, and a FLOAT FIRING/FLOAT FIRE pushbutton.
emergency-floatation-gear/0/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
emergency-floatation-gear/0/p0.note: RFM SUP.17 p.1 (1 GENERAL): approved for emergency use not ditching per JAR 27, keep upright/trimmed for evacuation, two floatation units parallel along each skid, 2 cylinders (1 per float) w/ pressure indicator, FLOAT ARM + FLOAT FIRING/FLOAT FIRE pushbuttons. Confirmed verbatim.

emergency-floatation-gear/1/note.context: System note 'Emergency Floatation Gear', section 'Limitations', table note
emergency-floatation-gear/1/note.text: Below 400 ft (122 m) over water, the gear must always be armed. Takeoff after an emergency landing on water is prohibited. Use only for emergency water landing — cylinder pressure limits are given on the adjacent placard.
emergency-floatation-gear/1/note.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
emergency-floatation-gear/1/note.note: RFM SUP.17 p.2: armed below 400ft over water, takeoff after emergency water landing prohibited, use only for emergency landing on water, placard adjacent to cylinder gives pressure limits. Confirmed verbatim.

emergency-floatation-gear/2/p0.context: System note 'Emergency Floatation Gear', section 'Inflation', paragraph
emergency-floatation-gear/2/p0.text: With FLOAT ARM pressed, if float inflation fails, continue flight and stay within gliding distance of the coastline — inflation is also impossible whenever MASTER SW/EMER SW is off. To inflate: press FLOAT ARM, confirm at least one of the FLOAT FIRING/FLOAT ARM lights is on, then press FLOAT FIRING/FLOAT FIRE — recommended below 80 kt IAS, since firing above that speed can produce a pitch-down deceleration.
emergency-floatation-gear/2/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
emergency-floatation-gear/2/p0.note: RFM SUP.17 p.3 (3 EMERGENCY PROCEDURES / INFLATION PROCEDURE): failure->continue flight within gliding distance of coastline, inflation impossible if MASTER SW/EMER SW off; press FLOAT ARM, check lights ON, press FLOAT FIRING/FLOAT FIRE, recommended below 80kt IAS (pitch-down risk above). Confirmed verbatim.

emergency-floatation-gear/3/p0.context: System note 'Emergency Floatation Gear', section 'Autorotation onto water', paragraph
emergency-floatation-gear/3/p0.text: Reduce collective to hold NR in the normal range, fly Vy. If relight is impossible, or after a tail rotor failure, set the engine starting selector OFF. Maneuver to head the aircraft between the wind and wave direction on final. At 70 ft, flare with cyclic. At 20–25 ft, holding constant attitude, gradually increase collective to reduce descent rate and forward speed. Then ease the cyclic slightly forward for a 10° nose-up attitude and under 10 kt forward speed at touchdown, adjusting pedals to cancel sideslip, and increase collective to cushion touchdown at minimum speed. After touchdown, lower collective fully, apply the rotor brake, and evacuate once the rotor has stopped — forward doors must be opened via the jettison handles once afloat.
emergency-floatation-gear/3/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
emergency-floatation-gear/3/p0.note: RFM SUP.17 p.4 (AUTOROTATION PROCEDURE OVER WATER): reduce collective/Vy, engine selector OFF if relight impossible/tail rotor failure, head between wind/wave, flare at 70ft, increase collective 20-25ft, forward cyclic for 10° nose-up <10kt touchdown, adjust pedals, cushion touchdown, decrease collective/rotor brake/evacuate, forward doors via jettison handles when afloat. Confirmed verbatim.

emergency-floatation-gear/4/p0.context: System note 'Emergency Floatation Gear', section 'Performance', paragraph
emergency-floatation-gear/4/p0.text: Stability after an emergency water landing was demonstrated up to a significant wave height of 2.5 m — sea state 4 on the World Meteorological Organization scale. Rate of climb is reduced by 50 ft/min (0.25 m/s) at Vy, and cruise speed by roughly 2 kt with the gear installed.
emergency-floatation-gear/4/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
emergency-floatation-gear/4/p0.note: RFM SUP.17 p.5 (5 PERFORMANCE DATA): stability demonstrated to 2.5m significant wave height (sea state 4 WMO), ROC reduced 50ft/min (0.25m/s) at Vy, cruise speed reduced ~2kt. Confirmed verbatim.

hoist-installation/0/note.context: System note 'Hoist Installation', section 'Two hoist families', table note
hoist-installation/0/note.text: Both share the same general architecture: a pivoting jib with a locking device (ferrying/hoisting positions) on the left side, a safety belt for the hoist operator, cable protectors on the LH skid, a hand-operated cable cutter as backup, and a pyrotechnic cable cutter. An 'up travel limit' detector cuts motor power when the hook is fully up; a 'down travel limit' cuts power with 4 m of cable left; a mechanical safety pin stops the drum at 3 m as a backup if the electrical down-limit fails.

hoist-installation/0/note.note: RFM SUP.18 p.1 (1.1 DESCRIPTION): pivoting jib w/ locking device, safety belt, cable protectors on LH skid, hand cable cutter, pyrotechnic cable cutter, up-travel-limit detector, down-travel-limit at 4m, mechanical safety pin at 3m. Confirmed verbatim.

hoist-installation/2/p0.text: Pilot: a HOIST pushbutton on the console to power the installation, and a guarded cable-shear pushbutton on the collective for emergency severing. bambi-bucket/0/p0.context: System note 'Bambi Bucket', section 'What it is', paragraph

sand-filter/0/p0.context: System note 'Sand Filter', section 'What it is', paragraph
sand-filter/0/p0.text: Protects the engine from sand ingestion during hover or flight in sand-laden air, and — without needing any bleed air for this function — also protects the air intake against snow ingestion while flying in falling snow. A filter sits on the engine air intake below the ice-protection screen; ambient air passes through separator tubes forming the filter, with filtered air forced toward the intake while sand is evacuated through scavenge tubes ventilated by P2 air. An electric valve, controlled by the SAND FILTER/SAND FILT pushbutton on the SCU, opens and closes the P2 air pressure circuit. A P2 message on the VEMD's FLI page confirms the valve is fully open.
sand-filter/0/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
sand-filter/0/p0.note: RFM SUP.14 p.1 (1 GENERAL): sand ingestion protection during hover/sandy air, also protects against snow ingestion without needing bleed air for that function, filter below ice-protection screen, separator tubes, scavenge tubes w/ P2 air, SAND FILTER/SAND FILT pushbutton on SCU, P2 message on VEMD FLI. Confirmed verbatim.

sand-filter/2/r0.note: RFM SUP.14 p.2 (emergency procedures): P2 remains off = valve fails to open, avoid sandy atmosphere. Confirmed verbatim.

sand-filter/3/p0.context: System note 'Sand Filter', section 'Operating notes', paragraph
sand-filter/3/p0.text: Preflight requires checking the engine air intake and filter are clean, with no ice/snow accumulation or foreign objects and no stagnant water at the drain hole — ice or snow left in or around the intake can be ingested and cause a sudden in-flight engine failure. Cycle SAND FILTER/SAND FILT on then off before starting the engine to confirm P2 responds on the VEMD. When actually flying in sandy conditions, select it ON with heating/demisting OFF.
sand-filter/3/p0.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
sand-filter/3/p0.note: RFM SUP.14 p.2/3 (normal procedures): exterior check clean/no ice-snow/no stagnant water, SAND FILTER ON then OFF checks before starting (P2 on VEMD each time), ON with heating/demisting OFF when flying in sand. Confirmed verbatim.

sand-filter/3/p1.context: System note 'Sand Filter', section 'Operating notes', paragraph
sand-filter/3/p1.text: Running the sand filter raises T4 by approximately 10°C — a normal, expected effect, not a fault. For the engine power check, run it with the sand filter OFF and use the dedicated power-check chart; the VEMD automatically adjusts its power-check and hover-performance calculations when the sand filter is fitted.
sand-filter/3/p1.source_rev: AS350 B3 2B1 Flight Manual, EASA certification, dated 10/01/2025
sand-filter/3/p1.note: RFM SUP.14 p.3 (performance data): t4 rises ~10°C running the filter, power check with filter OFF using dedicated chart, VEMD auto-adjusts power-check/hover-performance when filter fitted. Confirmed verbatim.
